BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.

- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged / internal – buyer positions only

---

## 1. Preliminary point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing

The Seller's preamble asserts that caps, baskets, periods and buyer-knowledge qualifiers were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "marked FINAL" and "not intended to be re-opened."

**Treat this as a negotiating assertion, not a fact.** Our playbook is explicit: the 20% cap and 18-month period are *conditional fallbacks* usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and **no such authority has been given**. Nothing in the Seller's package evidences any principal-level agreement on our side. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter at [11] actually undercuts the preamble: "No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included."

The "market context" paragraph (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months) is the Seller's characterisation of market and is also irrelevant to our mandate. **Recommendation:** respond in writing that no positions have been agreed at principal level, that the draft is a Seller proposal in all respects, and that our mark-up follows. Do not let the "FINAL" label stand unanswered, as silence may later be cited as acquiescence.

---

## 2. Clause-by-clause departures from playbook

### 2.1 Clause 12.1 – General Warranty cap
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Cap | 20% / AUD 4,800,000 | **25% / AUD 6,000,000** (opening); 20% only with Frost written authority – none given |

**Issue:** The Seller has drafted to our *unauthorised fallback*. This is a material departure and must be reversed to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. If the deal team wishes to concede 20% later, that requires Amelia Frost's written approval referencing this specific draft before we communicate it.

### 2.2 Clause 12.2 – Thresholds
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | **AUD 5,000** |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | **AUD 50,000** |
| Basket type | Deductible (excess only) | **Tipping – first-dollar once exceeded** |

**Issue:** Three simultaneous departures. The de minimis is 5x ours, the basket 5x ours, and – most significantly – the Seller has converted the basket from tipping to a deductible, which permanently removes AUD 250,000 of recovery. For a company whose known issues already include AUD 180,000 (Ironquay) and AUD 420,000 (bonuses), a deductible basket plus a high de minimis could wipe out a large portion of realistic claims. Push back on all three.

### 2.3 Clause 12.3 / 13 – Time limits and "all Claims unless stated otherwise"
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| General period | 18 months | **24 months**; 18 months only with Frost written approval – none given |
| Scope | "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | **Separate regimes**; no hidden general-regime override |

**Issue:** Two problems. First, 18 months is our unauthorised fallback and must be restored to 24 months. Second, and more dangerous, the drafting default ("applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise") is a **general-regime override**. It would sweep Title, Tax, IP, payment covenants and the specific indemnities under the general cap and time bar unless we remember to carve each one out. Reverse the default: limitations apply *only* to General Warranty Claims and *only* where expressly stated.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Regime | Same caps/time limits as general ("administrative simplicity") | **Separate regime**: 100% of price cap, ≥ 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar |

**Issue:** Unacceptable. Capacity and title go to whether we acquire anything at all. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept an AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month bar on a AUD 24m title failure. Restore the full fundamental regime.

### 2.5 Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature"
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct | Not carved out – caught by "all Claims of any nature" | **Carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance** to the maximum enforceable extent; non-waivable |

**Issue:** This is the most serious drafting point in the package. As drafted, the Seller's limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions would purport to apply even to fraudulent misrepresentation. Apart from being commercially unacceptable, such a provision is of doubtful enforceability and signals a seller seeking cover beyond the ordinary. Insert an express, non-waivable fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from every limitation (cap, de minimis, basket, time, exclusive remedy, non-reliance, buyer-knowledge). Also ensure the specific indemnities (Ironquay, bonuses if seller-funded, Riverlark) sit outside the exclusive-remedy and cap provisions.

### 2.6 Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – General disclosure
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | Whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012) + statutory registers + public records deemed disclosed | **Specific fair disclosure only**; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deeming |

**Issue:** Paragraphs [1.1] and [1.2] are exactly the blanket deeming our playbook rejects. Combined with Clause 8.3 (below), the Seller effectively says: "anything in the room or on a register is disclosed and known to you, so no claim." Replace with a "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter" standard, limited to the specific disclosures in section 2 onward. Paragraph [1.4] (no admission of anything) is tolerable as a standard reservation, but it should not be allowed to undermine the specific facts actually stated – those statements of fact (e.g., "has NOT been repaid") should be retained as they are useful to us.

### 2.7 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Qualifier | No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, **including anything discoverable** from data room or public records | **Delete blanket exclusion**; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named *Seller* knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities |

**Issue:** "Discoverable from the data room or public records" is a constructive/prudent-search knowledge standard, and extending it to "advisers" is broader still. It would gut the warranty package. Delete Clause 8.3 entirely. If a knowledge concept is to survive anywhere, it should operate only as a qualifier on specific warranties by reference to named Seller individuals after due enquiry.

### 2.8 Clause 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent (≈ AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue)
| | Seller Update | Seller Disclosure Letter [2] | Playbook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position | "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; satisfied on *delivery* of written consent | **No final written consent and no evidence conditions under cl. 11.3 are satisfied** | **Effective consent AND evidence cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied, before Completion**; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient |

**Issue:** The Update and the Disclosure Letter contradict each other. "Addressed" is not accurate when the Seller's own letter confirms nothing has been obtained. The consent-on-delivery mechanic is unacceptable for a customer representing ~30% of revenue: a consent letter that is itself conditional on cl. 11.3 conditions being met is not an effective consent. Require (a) a Condition Precedent that Bluefen's consent under cl. 11.2 is obtained in unconditional form or with all cl. 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied, (b) Buyer satisfaction (acting reasonably) with that evidence, and (c) at minimum "all reasonable endeavours" with specified steps, backed by the CP. Consider whether a Bluefen loss within 12 months should attract a price adjustment or specific indemnity as a fallback.

### 2.9 Clause 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility (≈ AUD 3.2m)
| | Seller Update | Disclosure Letter [3] | Playbook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position | Release "following Completion" | Not repaid; no discharge of security in data room | **Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective releases at Completion**. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval |

**Issue:** Post-completion release is a direct playbook breach. On a debt-free/cash-free deal we would be paying full price while the target remains encumbered and indebted. Require: a payout letter dated within a short window of Completion; repayment paid directly by the Buyer out of the Completion funds to Riverlark; executed deeds of release and PPSR discharges (or irrevocable undertaking to register them) delivered at Completion. Also confirm the change-of-control provision at cl. 8.1 is dealt with so the facility is not accelerated pre-Completion in a way that triggers default costs.

### 2.10 Funds flow – DD-005 employee bonuses (AUD 420,000 + on-costs)
| | Seller Update | Disclosure Letter [5] | Playbook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position | "A matter for the Seller"; not itemised | Not in funds flow; silent on payroll tax, super, on-costs | **Specific line item or seller-funded**; funds flow must not silently exclude |

**Issue:** "A matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless the SPA makes the Seller bear it. The bonuses are payable by the *Company* on Completion; if they are not in the funds flow and not treated as Debt or a Transaction Expense, the Buyer effectively funds them post-Completion. Require: (a) the AUD 420,000 plus employer superannuation, payroll tax and any other triggered on-costs to be itemised as a Transaction Expense / Debt-like item deducted from the price or paid by the Seller at Completion; (b) a specific indemnity for any shortfall; (c) the Seller to confirm the on-cost position in writing. Note the on-costs are currently unquantified – ask for the grossed-up figure.

### 2.11 Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP (SOW3 / AUD 180,000)
| | Seller Update | Disclosure Letter [4] | Playbook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Transfer of Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 open per DD-010; no receipt or assignment in room | **Broaden the indemnity**, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way |

**Issue:** The current indemnity covers only the payment itself. The real exposure is title to the Project Materials: under cl. 7.3, until every SOW3 fee has cleared, IP has not transferred. The indemnity must cover (a) the payment, (b) any claim by Ironquay, (c) costs of obtaining the confirmatory assignment, and (d) losses from any defect in title to or infringement in respect of the Project Materials. Preserve the cure: the Seller should procure payment and a confirmatory assignment before Completion, with the indemnity as back-stop. Note that neither we nor the Seller has verified the AUD 180,000 – request bank evidence of payment status.

### 2.12 Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 – DD-006 export/privacy incident (~1,240 records)
| | Seller Update | Disclosure Letter [6] | Playbook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position | "Preliminary operational matter"; "not expected to be material" | No determination of access, scope or notification duty; investigation preliminary; no loss figure | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; **assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way** |

**Issue:** The Update's "not expected to be material" is a conclusion the Seller's own letter says cannot yet be drawn. We should neither accept the Seller's downplaying nor overstate the matter. Require: a pre-Completion covenant to preserve all relevant logs and the download link audit trail; completion of the investigation (or a defined status report) before Completion; ongoing updates; a warranty that no notifiable data breach has occurred to the Seller's knowledge; and a specific indemnity for any notification costs, regulatory action or third-party claims arising from DD-006, uncapped by the general regime. Do not quantify a price adjustment at this stage.

### 2.13 Sandbar supplier renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000)
| | Seller Update | Disclosure Letter [8] | Playbook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position | Ordinary-course operating costs | Does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course | **Assess**; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction |

**Issue:** The Seller asserts "ordinary course" but its letter declines to commit to that. We should not automatically treat these as Debt, but we need the facts: contract terms, renewal dates, termination rights, whether the three are linked (DD-008/DD-011 "read together"), and whether any portion is accrued/payable pre-Completion. Depending on answers, treatment may range from nothing, through working-capital normalisation, to a Transaction Expense if the renewals were triggered by or accelerated for the sale. Hold position pending information.

### 2.14 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Position | Settled; subject to general cap/basket/time limits | **OPEN**; separate categories; no resolution; no unlimited liability |

**Issue:** Tax and IP are not settled and must not be folded into the 20%/18-month general regime by default (compounded by the 12.3/13 "all Claims" override). Respond that Tax and IP remain open for separate negotiation, with their own cap and period (likely longer than general, aligned to statutory review periods for Tax). We are not seeking unlimited liability; we are declining the Seller's premature closure.

### 2.15 Title – DD-012 share register
| | Seller Update | Disclosure Letter [10] | Playbook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position | Title evidenced by share register | Register is the source relied on; Buyer has not completed its own verification | **Independent** title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal document, not proof |

**Issue:** The Seller's own letter concedes DD-012 is merely "the source relied on." We need: ASIC extracts, share certificates, PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller for charges over the shares, evidence of Seller's corporate authority (board/shareholder approvals), and confirmation of no options, pre-emptive rights or shareholder agreements. This is independent DD work for us, plus a fundamental title warranty on the uncapped regime (see 2.4).

### 2.16 Other disclosures – lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
Not playbook items but worth noting: the Seller frames both as "notification only / not a consent requirement." Confirm by reviewing the actual clause wording ourselves rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation; if a notification is required, make it a pre-Completion covenant with evidence of delivery.

---

## 3. Observations on the overall package

1. **The Update overstates; the Disclosure Letter is more candid.** On Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006 and title, the Disclosure Letter contradicts or qualifies the confident language of the Update. We should cite the Seller's own letter back to them when rejecting the Update positions.
2. **The limitation architecture is built to collapse everything into one regime.** The combination of the Clause 13 "all Claims" default, Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 "any nature," fundamental warranties under general caps, whole-data-room disclosure, and the Clause 8.3 constructive-knowledge bar is cumulative. Each individually is bad; together they leave very little real warranty protection on a AUD 24m purchase.
3. **No evidence of any principal-level agreement.** Nothing supports the "FINAL" label, and internally we have no Frost authority for any fallback. Our mark-up should go out at opening positions.
4. **Debt-free/cash-free is not reflected in substance.** Riverlark unresolved at Completion plus unfunded bonuses means the Buyer would be paying headline price for a company still carrying ≈ AUD 3.6m+ of liabilities.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Topic | Our response |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Preamble | Reject "FINAL/settled" characterisation in writing; nothing is agreed |
| 2 | 12.1 Cap | Restore 25% / AUD 6,000,000; no fallback without Frost written authority |
| 3 | 12.2 Thresholds | De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **tipping** basket |
| 4 | 12.3/13 Period | 24 months; reverse the "all Claims unless stated" default |
| 5 | Fundamental/Title | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥ 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar |
| 6 | 9.3/12.8/20.5 | Non-waivable carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct from all limitations; specific indemnities outside exclusive remedy |
| 7 | Disclosure | Delete [1.1]/[1.2] blanket deeming; specific fair disclosure standard only |
| 8 | 8.3 Knowledge | Delete; any qualifier limited to named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud, indemnities |
| 9 | Bluefen | CP: effective consent + evidence cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied pre-Completion; not consent-on-delivery |
| 10 | Riverlark | Payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; releases at Completion; post-completion only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval |
| 11 | Bonuses | AUD 420,000 + super/payroll tax/on-costs as specific line item or seller-funded; indemnity for shortfall; request grossed-up figure |
| 12 | Ironquay | Broaden indemnity to title/claims/assignment costs; require payment + confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; verify the AUD 180,000 |
| 13 | DD-006 | Log preservation covenant; complete investigation/status report; updates; specific indemnity; no characterisation or quantification either way |
| 14 | Sandbar | Request contract terms; assess; no automatic Debt treatment or price reduction |
| 15 | Tax/IP | Reject "settled"; remain open as separate categories with their own cap and period |
| 16 | Title | Independent verification (ASIC, PPSR, certificates, authority docs); DD-012 is not proof |
| 17 | Lease/Mossvale | Verify clause wording ourselves; notification covenants where required |

**Internal action:** No fallback (20% cap, 18-month period, post-completion Riverlark release) is to be offered or accepted without Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. Suggest we send the mark-up at opening positions together with a cover note that formally records the absence of any principal-level agreement.

**Issue:** Unacceptable. Capacity and title go to whether we acquire anything at all. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept an AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month bar on a AUD 24m title failure. Restore the full fundamental regime.

### 2.5 Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature"
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct | Not carved out – caught by "all Claims of any nature" | **Carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance** to the maximum enforceable extent; non-waivable |

**Issue:** This is the most serious drafting point in the package. As drafted, the Seller's limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions would purport to apply even to fraudulent misrepresentation. Apart from being commercially unacceptable, such a provision is of doubtful enforceability and signals a seller seeking cover beyond the ordinary. Insert an express, non-waivable fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from every limitation (cap, de minimis, basket, time, exclusive remedy, non-reliance, buyer-knowledge). Also ensure the specific indemnities (Ironquay, bonuses if seller-funded, Riverlark) sit outside the exclusive-remedy and cap provisions.

### 2.6 Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – General disclosure
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | Whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012) + statutory registers + public records deemed disclosed | **Specific fair disclosure only**; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deeming |

**Issue:** Paragraphs [1.1] and [1.2] are exactly the blanket deeming our playbook rejects. Combined with Clause 8.3 (below), the Seller effectively says: "anything in the room or on a register is disclosed and known to you, so no claim." Replace with a "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter" standard, limited to the specific disclosures in section 2 onward. Paragraph [1.4] (no admission of anything) is tolerable as a standard reservation, but it should not be allowed to undermine the specific facts actually stated – those statements of fact (e.g., "has NOT been repaid") should be retained as they are useful to us.

### 2.7 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Qualifier | No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, **including anything discoverable** from data room or public records | **Delete blanket exclusion**; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named *Seller* knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities |

**Issue:** "Discoverable from the data room or public records" is a constructive/prudent-search knowledge standard, and extending it to "advisers" is broader still. It would gut the warranty package. Delete Clause 8.3 entirely. If a knowledge concept is to survive anywhere, it should operate only as a qualifier on specific warranties by reference to named Seller individuals after due enquiry.

### 2.8 Clause 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent (≈ AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue)
| | Seller Update | Seller Disclosure Letter [2] | Playbook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position | "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; satisfied on *delivery* of written consent | **No final written consent and no evidence conditions under cl. 11.3 are satisfied** | **Effective consent AND evidence cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied, before Completion**; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient |

**Issue:** The Update and the Disclosure Letter contradict each other. "Addressed" is not accurate when the Seller's own letter confirms nothing has been obtained. The consent-on-delivery mechanic is unacceptable for a customer representing ~30% of revenue: a consent letter that is itself conditional on cl. 11.3 conditions being met is not an effective consent. Require (a) a Condition Precedent that Bluefen's consent under cl. 11.2 is obtained in unconditional form or with all cl. 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied, (b) Buyer satisfaction (acting reasonably) with that evidence, and (c) at minimum "all reasonable endeavours" with specified steps, backed by the CP. Consider whether a Bluefen loss within 12 months should attract a price adjustment or specific indemnity as a fallback.

### 2.9 Clause 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility (≈ AUD 3.2m)
| | Seller Update | Disclosure Letter [3] | Playbook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position | Release "following Completion" | Not repaid; no discharge of security in data room | **Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective releases at Completion**. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval |

**Issue:** Post-completion release is a direct playbook breach. On a debt-free/cash-free deal we would be paying full price while the target remains encumbered and indebted. Require: a payout letter dated within a short window of Completion; repayment paid directly by the Buyer out of the Completion funds to Riverlark; executed deeds of release and PPSR discharges (or irrevocable undertaking to register them) delivered at Completion. Also confirm the change-of-control provision at cl. 8.1 is dealt with so the facility is not accelerated pre-Completion in a way that triggers default costs.

### 2.10 Funds flow – DD-005 employee bonuses (AUD 420,000 + on-costs)
| | Seller Update | Disclosure Letter [5] | Playbook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position | "A matter for the Seller"; not itemised | Not in funds flow; silent on payroll tax, super, on-costs | **Specific line item or seller-funded**; funds flow must not silently exclude |

**Issue:** "A matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless the SPA makes the Seller bear it. The bonuses are payable by the *Company* on Completion; if they are not in the funds flow and not treated as Debt or a Transaction Expense, the Buyer effectively funds them post-Completion. Require: (a) the AUD 420,000 plus employer superannuation, payroll tax and any other triggered on-costs to be itemised as a Transaction Expense / Debt-like item deducted from the price or paid by the Seller at Completion; (b) a specific indemnity for any shortfall; (c) the Seller to confirm the on-cost position in writing. Note the on-costs are currently unquantified – ask for the grossed-up figure.

### 2.11 Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP (SOW3 / AUD 180,000)

|---|---|---|---|
| Position | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Transfer of Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 open per DD-010; no receipt or assignment in room | **Broaden the indemnity**, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way |

**Issue:** The current indemnity covers only the payment itself. The real exposure is title to the Project Materials: under cl. 7.3, until every SOW3 fee has cleared, IP has not transferred. The indemnity must cover (a) the payment, (b) any claim by Ironquay, (c) costs of obtaining the confirmatory assignment, and (d) losses from any defect in title to or infringement in respect of the Project Materials. Preserve the cure: the Seller should procure payment and a confirmatory assignment before Completion, with the indemnity as back-stop. Note that neither we nor the Seller has verified the AUD 180,000 – request bank evidence of payment status.

### 2.12 Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 – DD-006 export/privacy incident (~1,240 records)

|---|---|---|---|
| Position | "Preliminary operational matter"; "not expected to be material" | No determination of access, scope or notification duty; investigation preliminary; no loss figure | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; **assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way** |

## 3. Observations on the overall package

1. **The Update overstates; the Disclosure Letter is more candid.** On Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006 and title, the Disclosure Letter contradicts or qualifies the confident language of the Update. We should cite the Seller's own letter back to them when rejecting the Update positions.
2. **The limitation architecture is built to collapse everything into one regime.** The combination of the Clause 13 "all Claims" default, Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 "any nature," fundamental warranties under general caps, whole-data-room disclosure, and the Clause 8.3 constructive-knowledge bar is cumulative. Each individually is bad; together they leave very little real warranty protection on a AUD 24m purchase.
3. **No evidence of any principal-level agreement.** Nothing supports the "FINAL" label, and internally we have no Frost authority for any fallback. Our mark-up should go out at opening positions.
4. **Debt-free/cash-free is not reflected in substance.** Riverlark unresolved at Completion plus unfunded bonuses means the Buyer would be paying headline price for a company still carrying ≈ AUD 3.6m+ of liabilities.
